chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Karram, who said:

I swore within myself that I would never eat food during the day until the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad rises. Then I entered upon Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and said to him: A man from your Shi'a has made it binding upon himself for Allah that he will not eat food during the day ever until the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad rises.

He said: Then fast, O Karram, but do not fast on the two Eids, nor the three days of al-Tashriq, nor when you are traveling, nor when ill. For when al-Husayn عليه السلام was killed, the heavens and the earth and those upon them and the angels cried out and said: Our Lord, grant us permission to destroy creation until we renew them from the face of the earth, because they violated Your sanctity and killed Your chosen one.

So Allah revealed to them: O My angels, O My heavens, and O My earth, be still. Then He uncovered a veil from among the veils, and behind it were Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his twelve legatees عليهم السلام, and He took the hand of that one, the Qa'im, from among them, and said: O My angels, O My heavens, and O My earth, by this one I shall grant victory for this one. He said it three times.

key_terms.اثْنَا عَشَرَ وَصِيًّا: the twelve successors designated after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام, whose martyrdom caused cosmic lamentation
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid days on which fasting is prohibited
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: the Qa'im عليه السلام through whom divine vengeance and vindication will occur
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ التَّشْرِيقِ: the three days of Tashriq during which fasting is not observed in this ruling
key_terms.صَفْوَتَكَ: Your chosen one; referring to the specially selected servant of Allah
key_terms.قَائِمُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the awaited Qa'im from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about fasting until the rise of al-Qa'im and the divine response to the martyrdom of al-Husayn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith combines a legal ruling with an eschatological and theological disclosure. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs Karram to observe his vowed daytime fasting within the limits of sacred law, then describes the cosmic reaction to the martyrdom of al-Husayn عليه السلام and Allah's promise of vindication through al-Qa'im عليه السلام from among the twelve successors.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhamad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Karram who said,

‘I took an oath regarding what is between me and myself that I will not eat food during the day, ever, until the ‘Qaim<sup>asws</sup> of the Progeny of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> rises. Then I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man from your<sup>asws</sup> Shias has Made it for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon him that he will not eat food by the day, ever, until the Qaim<sup>asws</sup> of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> rises’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Fast then O Karram, but do not Fast the two Eids, nor the three days of Al-Tashreek, nor when you are travelling, nor when sick, for Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> was murdered, the skies and the earth and the ones upon them and the Angels raised a clamour and they said, ‘O our Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Permit for us to destroy the people until we renew them with a new people on the earth due to that they have permitted Your<sup>azwj</sup> Sanctity (to be violated) and they murdered Your<sup>azwj</sup> elite’.

So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto them: “O My<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, and O My<sup>azwj</sup> skies, and O My<sup>azwj</sup> earth! Calm down!” Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Uncovered a Veil from the Veils, and there were behind it, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and twelve successors<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>saww</sup>, and Grabbed the hand of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> from between them<sup>asws</sup> and He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “O My<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, and O My<sup>azwj</sup> skies, and O My<sup>azwj</sup> earth! By this one<sup>asws</sup> I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Triumph for this one<sup>asws</sup>”. He<sup>azwj</sup> Said it three times’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from mmd ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from Karram who has said the following.

“I took an oath with my self that I will not any food during the day until the rise of Al-Qa’im (the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority). I then went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.).” The narrator has said, “A man from you Shi‘a (followers) has imposed on himself on oath not to eat any food during the day until the rise of Al-Qa’im from the family of Muhammad (s.a) (the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority).”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “Fast, then O Karram. Do not fast on the two ‘Id days and the three days of Tashriq (11,12,13) of the month of Dhil Hajj. Also do not fast when you are on a journey or when you will have an illness. It is because when al-Husayn was murdered the heavens and the earth and all the angles in them mourned and lamented before the Lord. They said, “Lord, grant us permission to destroy the creature and purge the earth from them because of their disregard of you reverence and their murdering your chosen people.

Allah then inspired them, “My angels, My heavens and My earth be patient and relieved.. He then removed a barrier of the barriers and there appeared Muhammad and the twelve executors of his will. He then held the hand of so and so, Al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine Authority) from among them and said, ‘O My angels, My heavens and My earth through this I will grant support for this.” He said it three times.”
